0.long_answer: Metformin is an oral anti-diabetic medication that has been shown to be more effective than insulin in reducing the incidence of fetal macrosomia in pregnant patients. Studies indicate that metformin not only helps control maternal hyperglycemia but also leads to a significantly lower risk (approximately 20% lower chance) of delivering a large-for-gestational-age baby compared to insulin therapy. This makes it a preferred option in certain cases of gestational diabetes management where reducing the risk of fetal overgrowth is a key treatment goal.
